Tanaka et al. disclosed the Rh(I)-catalyzed stereo-
selective additions of chloroformate with allenes
yielding 3-chloro-3(Z)-alkenoates 708 and 709 with
a regioselectivity of >91% via chlororhodation and a
reductive elimination mechanism. The reaction of
phenylallene is low-yielding and much less regiose-
lective (Scheme 145).

9. Carbometalation Reactions
Cheng et al. demonstrated the carbopalladation-
â-H elimination process for the efficient synthesis of
1,3-dienes 710-712. 4-Acyl(or nitro)phenyl chloride
yielded the products in 21 -29% yields. Alkenyl
bromides shown in Scheme 126 could also be applied
for this transformation. The reaction with 1-phenyl-
1,2-butadiene or cyclohexylpropadiene yielded regioi-
someric mixtures. In addition, the stereoselectivity
of this reaction is poor (Scheme 146).
171
This Pd(0)-catalyzed reaction of aryl halides with
allenes usually ended up with the formation of a
ð-allyl palladium intermediate, which may also un-
dergo Tsuji-Trost-type chemistry with nucleophiles.
172
Grigg et al. reported the efficient synthesis of R,â-
unsaturated E-enamides from the acylpalladation of
allenes in the presence of an amine (Scheme 147).173
The Pd(0)-catalyzed four-component reaction of
aryl halide, CO, amine, and a polymer-supported
allene 714 leading to the highly selective formation
of 2-acyl allylic amines 715 has also been disclosed
(Scheme 148).174
An intermolecular carbopalladation of propadiene
then intermolecular allylic substitution with tosyl-
amines
175a-e bearing a terminal C dC bond afforded
a diene 716, which would undergo a RCM reaction
to afford N-heterocycles (Scheme 149). 175f
A three-component reaction of aryl halides, propa-
diene, and 4-hydroxycoumarin718 was conducted in
a Schlenk tube to afford C-allylation products 719,
which undergo further cyclization under the catalysis
of TFA to afford tricyclic product 720.
